series_description: A complete weekly training series taking you from AI beginner to senior AI engineer. Published every Saturday morning on The Data and AI School of London YouTube channel.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Roadmap 2026: Zero to Master
episodes.og_description: The complete roadmap to becoming a senior AI engineer in 2026. Skills, tools, frameworks and career path from beginner to master.
episodes.image_prompt: Futuristic roadmap showing AI engineering career journey, glowing connected path from beginner to expert level, neural network patterns as background, London skyline silhouette, professional navy blue and gold colour scheme, photorealistic
episodes.content_brief: What AI Engineering is and how it differs from data science and software engineering. The complete skill tree: Python foundations, mathematics for AI, classical machine learning, deep learning, large language models, MLOps and production systems. Tools and frameworks at each stage. Recommended learning order with realistic timeline milestones. UK job market: roles, salaries and demand in 2026. How this series is structured and what each episode covers.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 1: Setting Up Your AI Development Environment
episodes.og_description: Set up a professional AI engineering workspace from scratch. Python, VS Code, Jupyter, Git, virtual environments and GPU setup covered step by step.
episodes.image_prompt: Modern professional developer workspace with multiple monitors showing code, terminal and Jupyter notebooks, clean desk setup with keyboard and coffee, dark theme editors, tech-forward atmosphere, navy blue and gold tones
episodes.content_brief: Installing Python 3.11 correctly on Windows, Mac and Linux. Setting up VS Code with essential AI/ML extensions. Creating and managing virtual environments with conda and venv. Jupyter notebooks and JupyterLab setup. Git and GitHub basics for AI projects. GPU drivers and CUDA setup for deep learning. Essential Python libraries: NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Scikit-learn, PyTorch. Verifying the environment works end to end.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 2: Python Fundamentals Every AI Engineer Must Know
episodes.og_description: Master the Python skills essential for AI engineering. NumPy, list comprehensions, OOP, decorators, generators and writing clean Pythonic code.
episodes.image_prompt: Python code on a large monitor with colourful syntax highlighting, abstract Python logo integrated with AI neural network visualisation, clean professional workspace, navy and gold accents
episodes.content_brief: Python data structures for AI: lists, dicts, sets and their performance characteristics. NumPy arrays vs Python lists: why AI engineers use NumPy. List comprehensions and generator expressions for efficient data processing. Object-oriented Python: classes, inheritance and why it matters for ML frameworks. Decorators and context managers used in AI libraries. Type hints and how to write readable AI code. Common Python mistakes AI engineers make and how to avoid them. Writing unit tests for AI utility functions.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 3: Linear Algebra for AI Engineers
episodes.og_description: Learn the linear algebra every AI engineer needs. Vectors, matrices, dot products, eigenvalues and how they power neural networks and machine learning.
episodes.image_prompt: Elegant mathematical visualisation of matrices and vectors transforming in space, 3D geometric shapes, clean academic illustration style, navy blue background with gold mathematical symbols and grid lines
episodes.content_brief: Scalars, vectors and matrices: intuitive understanding and Python implementation. Matrix multiplication and why it is the core operation of neural networks. Dot products and their geometric interpretation. Transpose, inverse and identity matrices. Norms and distance measures in machine learning. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors: what they mean and where they appear in PCA and attention. Broadcasting in NumPy. Practical exercises computing forward passes through simple neural network layers using only NumPy.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 4: Calculus, Probability and Statistics for AI
episodes.og_description: The calculus and statistics every AI engineer needs. Derivatives, gradient descent, probability distributions, Bayes theorem and statistical thinking for ML.
episodes.image_prompt: Abstract visualisation of gradient descent on a 3D loss surface with glowing optimisation path reaching the minimum, mathematical curves and probability bell curves floating in background, navy and gold professional palette
episodes.content_brief: Derivatives and partial derivatives: the mathematical foundation of learning. The chain rule and how it enables backpropagation. Gradient descent intuition with 2D and 3D visualisations. Learning rates and why they matter. Probability distributions: uniform, Gaussian, Bernoulli and Categorical. Bayes theorem and probabilistic thinking in ML. Expected values, variance and standard deviation. Hypothesis testing and p-values in model evaluation. Information theory: entropy, cross-entropy loss and KL divergence.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 5: Machine Learning Fundamentals
episodes.og_description: Master machine learning fundamentals. Supervised vs unsupervised learning, the bias-variance tradeoff, overfitting, cross-validation and scikit-learn workflows.
episodes.image_prompt: Machine learning concept visualisation: decision boundaries separating coloured data clusters on a 2D plot, model evaluation metrics dashboard, professional data science workspace, navy and gold colour scheme
episodes.content_brief: What machine learning is and when to use it versus rule-based systems. Supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning. The machine learning workflow: data, features, training, evaluation, deployment. Bias-variance tradeoff and what it means for your models. Overfitting and underfitting: recognition and solutions. Train, validation and test splits. Cross-validation techniques. Key evaluation metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC-ROC, RMSE. The scikit-learn API: fit, predict, transform. Building a complete end-to-end ML pipeline.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 6: Supervised Learning In Depth
episodes.og_description: Deep dive into supervised learning algorithms. Linear regression, logistic regression, decision trees, random forests, gradient boosting and XGBoost with Python.
episodes.image_prompt: Side-by-side visual comparison of multiple machine learning model decision boundaries on scattered datasets, clean data visualisation style, algorithm comparison chart, professional tech aesthetic, navy blue tones
episodes.content_brief: Linear regression from scratch and with scikit-learn. Regularisation: Ridge, Lasso and ElasticNet. Logistic regression for classification. Decision trees: splitting criteria, depth and pruning. Random forests: why ensembles work. Gradient boosting: AdaBoost, GBM, XGBoost and LightGBM. Feature importance and model interpretability. Hyperparameter tuning with GridSearchCV and Optuna. When to use which algorithm: a practical decision guide. Handling imbalanced datasets.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 7: Unsupervised Learning and Clustering
episodes.og_description: Master unsupervised learning. K-means, DBSCAN, hierarchical clustering, PCA dimensionality reduction, autoencoders and anomaly detection with Python.
episodes.image_prompt: Colourful 3D data clusters visualised in space, dimensionality reduction from high-dimensional to 2D scatter plot, abstract data visualisation art, professional navy and gold colour palette, no text
episodes.content_brief: When to use unsupervised learning. K-means clustering: algorithm, choosing K, limitations. DBSCAN for density-based clustering. Hierarchical clustering and dendrograms. Evaluation metrics for clustering: silhouette score, Davies-Bouldin index. Principal Component Analysis: intuition, implementation and when to use it. t-SNE and UMAP for visualisation. Autoencoders: architecture and applications. Anomaly detection techniques. Real-world use cases: customer segmentation, fraud detection, recommendation systems.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 8: Neural Networks from Scratch
episodes.og_description: Build neural networks from scratch using only NumPy. Forward pass, backpropagation, activation functions and gradient descent implemented step by step.
episodes.image_prompt: Illuminated neural network diagram with glowing nodes and connections showing forward and backward pass data flow, dark background with navy and gold colour scheme, technical and elegant scientific illustration
episodes.content_brief: What a neuron does mathematically. Layers: input, hidden and output. Activation functions: sigmoid, ReLU, tanh, softmax and when to use each. Forward pass implementation in NumPy. Loss functions: mean squared error and cross-entropy. Backpropagation: the chain rule applied step by step. Weight initialisation strategies: Xavier and He initialisation. Gradient descent, mini-batch SGD and momentum. Implementing a complete two-layer network to classify MNIST digits. Why we moved from hand-coded to frameworks.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 9: Deep Learning with PyTorch
episodes.og_description: Learn deep learning with PyTorch. Tensors, autograd, nn.Module, DataLoaders, training loops, GPU acceleration and building your first deep neural network.
episodes.image_prompt: PyTorch logo integrated into glowing neural network architecture diagram, GPU acceleration visual with data flowing through deep network layers, modern tech development environment, navy and gold professional theme
episodes.content_brief: Why PyTorch became the standard for AI research and production. Tensors: creation, operations and GPU transfer. Autograd: automatic differentiation and computational graphs. Building models with nn.Module and nn.Sequential. DataLoaders and custom Datasets for efficient batching. The training loop: forward pass, loss, backward, optimiser step. Optimisers: SGD, Adam, AdamW. Learning rate schedulers. Saving and loading models. Debugging common PyTorch errors. GPU training on Google Colab and cloud platforms.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 10: Natural Language Processing Foundations
episodes.og_description: Learn NLP from the ground up. Tokenisation, embeddings, TF-IDF, word2vec, sentiment analysis and text classification before the era of transformers.
episodes.image_prompt: Abstract text processing visualisation: words transforming into numerical vectors and embeddings, language processing neural network, book with floating data and semantic connections, navy and gold professional colour scheme
episodes.content_brief: What NLP is and the range of tasks it covers. Text preprocessing: tokenisation, stemming, lemmatisation, stopword removal. Bag of words and TF-IDF representations. Word embeddings: word2vec, GloVe and FastText. Training a text classifier with scikit-learn. Named entity recognition and part-of-speech tagging. Text similarity and cosine distance. Practical project: building a spam detector. Limitations of pre-transformer NLP and why transformers changed everything.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 11: Transformers and the Attention Mechanism Explained
episodes.og_description: Understand how transformers work. Self-attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding, encoder-decoder architecture and implementing attention in PyTorch.
episodes.image_prompt: Elegant transformer architecture diagram with attention patterns visualised as heatmaps, coloured attention heads showing relationships between tokens, mathematical elegance in navy and gold scientific illustration style
episodes.content_brief: The problem with RNNs that transformers solved. The attention mechanism intuition: which words should attend to which. Queries, keys and values: the mathematical formulation. Scaled dot-product attention step by step. Multi-head attention and why it helps. Positional encoding: giving order to unordered attention. The encoder and decoder stacks. Layer normalisation and residual connections. BERT and GPT as examples of encoder-only and decoder-only variants. Implementing a single attention head in PyTorch.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 12: How Large Language Models Really Work
episodes.og_description: Demystify large language models. Pre-training, tokenisation, next-token prediction, RLHF, context windows, hallucinations and the inner workings of GPT-4 and Claude.
episodes.image_prompt: Inside a large language model: glowing transformer layers, token sequences flowing through the network, vast parameter space visualised as illuminated constellation, professional tech editorial style, navy and gold
episodes.content_brief: What an LLM is at its core: a next-token predictor. The pre-training process: data, compute and scale. Tokenisation: BPE and how text becomes numbers. The role of the context window. Instruction tuning: going from language model to assistant. Reinforcement learning from human feedback. Why LLMs hallucinate and what AI engineers can do about it. Model size, context length and capability trade-offs. Open-weight vs proprietary models: GPT-4, Claude 3.5, Llama 3, Mistral, Gemini. Choosing the right LLM for your use case.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 13: Prompt Engineering Mastery
episodes.og_description: Master prompt engineering for production AI systems. Zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, system prompts, structured output and prompt testing techniques.
episodes.image_prompt: Elegant visualisation of prompt engineering: human text input transforming through LLM to precise structured output, chain-of-thought reasoning steps visualised as glowing nodes, professional navy and gold tech palette
episodes.content_brief: What prompt engineering is and why AI engineers must master it. Zero-shot, one-shot and few-shot prompting. Designing effective system prompts. Chain-of-thought prompting for reasoning tasks. ReAct prompting for agentic workflows. Structured output: getting JSON from LLMs reliably. Prompt templating with Jinja2. Testing and evaluating prompts systematically. Common prompt engineering mistakes and how to avoid them. Role prompting, persona assignment and tone control. Prompt injection and security considerations.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 14: Building RAG Applications from Scratch
episodes.og_description: Build production-ready RAG systems from scratch. Chunking, embedding, vector search, context injection and advanced RAG techniques with Python and open-source tools.
episodes.image_prompt: Retrieval Augmented Generation architecture diagram: document corpus transforming to vectors in database, query flowing through retrieval to LLM generating accurate answer, glowing pipeline visualisation, navy and gold
episodes.content_brief: What RAG is, why it was invented and when to use it over fine-tuning. The complete RAG pipeline: ingestion, chunking, embedding, indexing, retrieval and generation. Document loading with different file types (PDF, DOCX, HTML). Chunking strategies: fixed size, recursive, semantic. Embedding models: OpenAI, Cohere, sentence-transformers. Vector similarity search: cosine, dot product, Euclidean. Building naive RAG in pure Python. Evaluating RAG: faithfulness, relevance and context recall. Advanced RAG: HyDE, reranking, parent-child chunking.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 15: Vector Databases: Pinecone, Chroma and Weaviate
episodes.og_description: Master vector databases for AI applications. Compare Pinecone, Chroma, Weaviate and pgvector. Indexing, querying, filtering metadata and production deployment.
episodes.image_prompt: Abstract vector database visualisation: high-dimensional vectors mapped in 3D space with similarity clustering, database architecture diagram with glowing indices, professional tech infographic style, navy and gold
episodes.content_brief: Why traditional databases fail for similarity search. How vector indices work: HNSW and IVF. Comparing options: Pinecone (managed), Chroma (local/open-source), Weaviate (hybrid), pgvector (PostgreSQL extension), Qdrant. Setting up Chroma locally for development. Indexing documents with metadata. Hybrid search: combining vector and keyword search. Filtering by metadata at query time. Production considerations: latency, throughput and cost. Migrating from local Chroma to managed Pinecone. Monitoring and optimising vector search performance.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 16: Fine-tuning LLMs with LoRA and QLoRA
episodes.og_description: Fine-tune large language models efficiently with LoRA and QLoRA. Domain adaptation, instruction tuning and training Llama 3 on a consumer GPU with Hugging Face.
episodes.image_prompt: LLM fine-tuning visualisation: base model with LoRA adapter matrices highlighted, training loss curve decreasing, Hugging Face and transformer logos integrated into professional tech diagram, navy and gold colour scheme
episodes.content_brief: When to fine-tune vs RAG vs prompt engineering. Full fine-tuning vs parameter-efficient methods. LoRA: the intuition and mathematics behind low-rank adaptation. QLoRA: quantisation-aware fine-tuning to fit large models on smaller GPUs. Hugging Face ecosystem: transformers, PEFT and TRL libraries. Preparing a training dataset: format, size and quality requirements. Training configuration: learning rate, batch size, epochs and early stopping. Evaluating fine-tuned models: perplexity, downstream task benchmarks. Merging LoRA weights and deploying the fine-tuned model.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 17: Building AI Applications with LangChain
episodes.og_description: Build powerful AI applications with LangChain. Chains, prompts, memory, document loaders, retrievers and deploying production LangChain apps with LangSmith.
episodes.image_prompt: LangChain application architecture: interconnected chain components visualised as glowing modular blocks, agent reasoning steps shown as flowing decision nodes, professional AI application diagram, navy and gold
episodes.content_brief: What LangChain is and when it is the right tool. Core abstractions: LLMs, chat models, prompt templates and output parsers. LangChain Expression Language (LCEL): composing chains declaratively. Memory types: ConversationBufferMemory, ConversationSummaryMemory. Document loaders and text splitters. Retrievers and RetrievalQA chains. Building a conversational RAG app step by step. LangChain agents and built-in tools. LangSmith for tracing, debugging and evaluating production apps. Common LangChain pitfalls and when to avoid it entirely.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 18: Document Intelligence with LlamaIndex
episodes.og_description: Master LlamaIndex for document intelligence and enterprise RAG. Indices, query engines, agents, sub-questions and building multi-document AI assistants in Python.
episodes.image_prompt: LlamaIndex document intelligence pipeline: multiple document types flowing into indices, complex query splitting into sub-questions, synthesised answer emerging, clean technical architecture diagram, navy and gold
episodes.content_brief: LlamaIndex vs LangChain: choosing the right framework. Core concepts: documents, nodes, indices and query engines. VectorStoreIndex for semantic search. SummaryIndex for summarisation over long documents. Knowledge graph index. Sub-question query engine for complex multi-hop questions. Metadata filtering and post-retrieval reranking. Router query engine for routing between indices. Building a multi-document research assistant. Response synthesis modes. LlamaIndex in production: caching, persistence and async queries.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 19: AI Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
episodes.og_description: Build autonomous AI agents and multi-agent systems. ReAct agents, tool calling, planning, memory, AutoGen multi-agent workflows and production agent architecture.
episodes.image_prompt: Multi-agent system visualisation: multiple AI agent nodes communicating and collaborating, orchestrator routing tasks between specialised agents, glowing decision trees and action sequences, navy and gold tech diagram
episodes.content_brief: What AI agents are and how they differ from chains. The ReAct framework: reason, act, observe loop. Tool use: giving agents access to search, code execution and APIs. Planning patterns: CoT, tree-of-thought and plan-and-execute. Memory in agents: short-term, long-term and episodic. Multi-agent architectures: supervisor, collaboration and debate. Building a research agent with LangGraph. AutoGen for multi-agent conversations. Agent evaluation: task completion rate, efficiency and error recovery. Production challenges: cost, latency and reliability.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 20: Function Calling and Tool Use with LLMs
episodes.og_description: Master function calling and tool use with modern LLMs. Defining tools for OpenAI, Anthropic and Google APIs. Parallel tool calls, error handling and building tool-augmented AI systems.
episodes.image_prompt: Function calling architecture: LLM receiving user request, identifying required function, executing tool call and integrating result back into response, clean modular API diagram, navy and gold professional style
episodes.content_brief: What function calling is and why it replaced prompt hacking for tool use. Defining tools in JSON schema for OpenAI, Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini APIs. The function calling loop: model decision, extraction, execution, result injection. Parallel tool calls for efficiency. Strict mode for guaranteed schema adherence. Building a tool library: web search, code execution, database queries, API calls. Error handling when tool execution fails. Streaming with function calls. Building a complete AI assistant with five tools end to end.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 21: Working with AI APIs: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google
episodes.og_description: Master the major AI APIs in 2026. OpenAI GPT-4, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini: authentication, rate limits, cost optimisation, streaming, batch processing and error handling.
episodes.image_prompt: Three major AI API providers visualised as interconnected hubs with API request and response data flowing between developer application and cloud AI services, professional technical diagram, navy and gold
episodes.content_brief: Setting up and authenticating with OpenAI, Anthropic and Google AI APIs. API key management and security best practices. Comparing models: GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro. Context windows, pricing and latency benchmarks. Streaming responses for better user experience. Async API calls for throughput. Batch APIs for cost reduction on large workloads. Rate limit handling with exponential backoff and retries. Caching strategies to reduce API costs. Fallback strategies when an API is down. Monitoring token usage and costs in production.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 22: Building Production AI APIs with FastAPI
episodes.og_description: Build production-ready AI APIs with FastAPI. Streaming endpoints, async LLM calls, authentication, rate limiting, caching and deploying your AI API to the cloud.
episodes.image_prompt: FastAPI server architecture diagram: incoming API requests processed through authentication middleware, routed to AI inference endpoints, responses streamed back to clients, clean technical illustration, navy and gold
episodes.content_brief: Why FastAPI is the standard for AI API development. Project structure for production AI APIs. Async endpoints for non-blocking LLM calls. Server-Sent Events for streaming AI responses to frontends. Request validation with Pydantic models. API key authentication middleware. Rate limiting with Redis and slowapi. Response caching for repeated queries. Background tasks for async processing. Dependency injection for shared resources (LLM clients, DB connections). Error handling and logging. Health check and metrics endpoints. Testing FastAPI AI endpoints.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 23: Containerising and Deploying AI Applications
episodes.og_description: Deploy AI applications with Docker and cloud platforms. Writing Dockerfiles for AI apps, Docker Compose, GPU containers, deploying to AWS, GCP and Azure.
episodes.image_prompt: Containerisation and cloud deployment visualisation: Docker containers shipping from local development to cloud infrastructure, orchestration layer managing AI model serving, modern DevOps aesthetic, navy and gold
episodes.content_brief: Why containerisation is essential for AI applications. Writing efficient Dockerfiles for Python AI apps. Multi-stage builds to keep images small. Docker Compose for local development with GPU support. NVIDIA Container Toolkit for GPU access in Docker. Environment variable management and secrets in containers. Cloud deployment options: AWS ECS, Google Cloud Run, Azure Container Apps. Kubernetes basics for AI workloads. Auto-scaling AI inference endpoints. Cost optimisation: spot instances and serverless inference. CI/CD pipeline for automated AI deployment.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 24: MLOps and CI/CD for Machine Learning
episodes.og_description: Implement MLOps practices for production AI. Experiment tracking with MLflow, model versioning, automated testing, CI/CD pipelines and model registry workflows.
episodes.image_prompt: MLOps pipeline visualisation: data flowing through training, experiment tracking, model registry, CI/CD stages to production deployment, continuous monitoring feedback loop, professional DevOps diagram, navy and gold
episodes.content_brief: What MLOps is and why it matters for AI engineers. The ML lifecycle: data, experiment, train, evaluate, deploy, monitor. Experiment tracking with MLflow: logging metrics, parameters and artefacts. Model versioning and the model registry. Automated model testing: unit tests, integration tests and data validation. Feature stores: what they are and when you need one. CI/CD for ML with GitHub Actions. Canary deployments and A/B testing models. Data and model drift detection. Reproducibility: seeds, environments and dataset versioning. Building an end-to-end MLOps workflow from scratch.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 25: Model Monitoring and Observability in Production
episodes.og_description: Monitor AI models in production. Data drift, concept drift, LLM output quality monitoring, Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards and alerting for AI systems.
episodes.image_prompt: AI model monitoring dashboard with real-time metrics, drift detection alerts, quality score trends and production inference logs on multiple screens, professional operations centre aesthetic, navy and gold
episodes.content_brief: Why models degrade in production and the types of drift. Infrastructure monitoring vs model performance monitoring. Metrics to track: latency, throughput, error rate, prediction distributions. Data drift detection: statistical tests and reference datasets. LLM-specific monitoring: hallucination rates, output quality, toxicity and cost per request. LangSmith and Langfuse for LLM observability. Setting up Prometheus and Grafana for AI metrics. Alerting strategies: when to retrain vs when to roll back. Log aggregation with the ELK stack. Building a monitoring system for a production RAG application.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 26: AI Safety, Ethics and Responsible AI in Practice
episodes.og_description: Build safe and ethical AI systems. Bias detection, fairness metrics, red teaming, guardrails, AI safety frameworks, UK AI regulation and responsible deployment practices.
episodes.image_prompt: AI safety and ethics visualisation: balanced scales with AI power and human oversight, protective guardrails around AI system, UK regulatory documents integrated with technology, responsible thoughtful atmosphere, navy and gold
episodes.content_brief: What AI safety means for engineers (not just researchers). Types of AI harm: bias, privacy, security, misuse and autonomy risks. Bias detection and fairness metrics for classification models. Fairness trade-offs and the impossibility theorem. Red teaming LLMs: adversarial prompting, jailbreaks and prompt injection. Adding guardrails to AI systems: NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI. Content moderation and output filtering. UK AI regulation: the AI Act, ICO guidance and sector-specific rules. Privacy-preserving ML: federated learning and differential privacy. Building an AI ethics review checklist for production systems.

episodes.title: AI Engineering Ep 27: Senior AI Engineer Career Path and Portfolio
episodes.og_description: Launch your AI engineering career. Build a standout portfolio, ace technical interviews, understand UK AI engineer salaries, and plan your path to senior AI engineer.
episodes.image_prompt: Career progression visualisation for AI engineers: ascending path with portfolio projects, GitHub contributions, UK tech company logos, salary benchmarks and job title milestones, optimistic professional imagery, navy and gold
episodes.content_brief: What distinguishes a senior AI engineer from a junior: technical depth, system design and business impact. Building a portfolio of six projects covering the full stack (ML, LLM, RAG, MLOps, deployment). GitHub profile optimisation for AI roles. Writing an AI engineer CV that passes ATS and impresses hiring managers. Technical interview preparation: system design, coding, ML theory and LLM questions. UK AI engineer salaries in 2026: junior, mid and senior bands in London and remotely. Top UK companies hiring AI engineers. Freelancing and consulting in AI. Your next steps as a DAIS graduate.
